# Site-symmetry lifecycle reference

`generate.py` selects the committed cctbx-base 2026.8 subspace table from
`tests/fixtures/anisotropic_adps/cctbx-subspaces.tsv`. That table's visible
`generate.py` obtains each Wyckoff stabilizer and ADP constraints independently
from cctbx, at two generic representatives; it never imports crysta or edi.
The selected reference records the complete table digest. No product-generated
tensor is a correctness oracle here.

The selected rows are Pm-3m a (m-3m), P4/mmm a (4/mmm), P6/mmm a (6/mmm), and
P1 a (general position). Their ranks and all U/B/beta basis coefficients are
read from the table. The general cell is nonorthogonal. Two different atoms
occupy the same representative with different ADP values, reproducing the
reported same-position ownership boundary. The GUI vehicles are generated by
the same writer and have no app build step.

The completion oracle solves the independently supplied tensor basis at the
editable components. It permits any independent component choice except the
owner's explicit cubic ani11 seed. Representation changes use corresponding
cctbx basis columns, including anisotropic inputs with unequal allowed
components. Ueq/Beq is the full Cartesian trace expressed through the direct
cell metric; beta uses its reciprocal tensor representation. Cross-term and
missing-follower controls exercise the oracle before any product assertion.

Fit profiles calculated by the engine are explicitly stimuli for moving a
selected parameter. Correctness is the table subspace, full-tensor equivalent,
fixed other-site preservation and successful completion, not diffraction
accuracy claimed from those calculated intensities.

Regenerate both mirrors and GUI inputs with:

```sh
python tests/fixtures/adp_site_symmetry/generate.py \
  --table tests/fixtures/anisotropic_adps/cctbx-subspaces.tsv \
  --output tests/fixtures/adp_site_symmetry \
  --output ../edi/tests/fixtures/adp_site_symmetry
```

The edi fit-site registry associates this lifecycle observation with the declared
LBCO corpus case lbco-hrpt-s4. The boundary stimuli are explicitly synthetic,
independently constrained tensors; no synthetic profile asserts diffraction
accuracy or replaces the corpus fitting oracle.
